items.english: "..." He wanted to say, I haven't the least idea what any of it is about, eh. What they call realism he didn't understand, and gutai and kuutai and that he didn't understand either, so he only thought of that konnyaku question-and-answer of the rakugo man.
notes: Left genjitsu-shugi as realism and gutai/kuutai as sound kept in roman, to match concrete in p116 and to leave his non-understanding visible; left konnyaku question-and-answer unglossed per style.

items.english: In the meantime two or three more novels seemed to come up for discussion, but they did not take his interest the way the tiger had, so with his eyes on the Western picture he could make nothing of hanging on the wall to the right of where he sat and on the gilt lettering of the books in the bookcase knocked together out of beer crates to his front left, he bit back the yawns that kept coming. The host did say, We had better give Nekohachi some sake, but, "No, I am more for the katsubushi side," he answered, and had mochi cakes brought out by the host's wife. And as he talked with her about the pleasure of growing vegetables and about the bringing up of each other's children, he got two or three magazines the children looked likely to read.
notes: Joined p119-p120 as one English sentence group since p119 ends mid-clause on keredomo; kept katsubushi literally though unsure whether snack, side dish, or set phrase for declining drink, rather than smoothing to sweets.

items.english: Then from Takami-san, "Well, let us have you do something, eh."

"..." Now this from here on was at last his own world, he thought, and the damp feeling he had got from the tiger story went off somewhere, and he wanted them to think better of his art than of the tiger. He had righted himself before he knew it, and in his readiness there was the same braced spirit as on the kouza, and before he had yet done anything he could hear his own mimic voice. He bent the little finger of his right hand like a hook and started to carry it to his just opened mouth, then stopped and looked the finger over, half to himself, "Sweaty and short of oil, I wonder if it will go, eh."

data.say: Drafted p118 to p123 as ramble and stage preparation without tidying the long sentences.
